  "plan": "# Flexbox Align Properties Lab Post\n\n## Context\n\n- Labs live in [src/content/labs/](src/content/labs/) as &#96;.mdx&#96; files\n- Content collection auto-discovers them; routing is &#96;/l/{slug}&#96; (slug = filename without extension)\n- Schema requires: &#96;title&#96;, &#96;description&#96;, optional &#96;badge&#96;, optional &#96;draft&#96;\n- Existing labs ([interpolate-size.mdx](src/content/labs/interpolate-size.mdx), [css-layer.mdx](src/content/labs/css-layer.mdx)) share a common structure\n\n## Structure to Follow (from css-layer.mdx)\n\n1. **Frontmatter**: &#96;title&#96;, &#96;description&#96;, &#96;badge: \"CSS\"&#96;\n2. **Wrapper**: &#96;\u003cdiv class=\"max-w-5xl mx-auto space-y-10\"\u003e&#96;\n3. **Header**: Centered title with &#96;\u003ccode\u003e&#96; styling, description paragraph\n4. **Explanatory section**: &#96;\u003csection class=\"space-y-6 max-w-3xl mx-auto\"\u003e&#96; with &#96;h2&#96; headings and paragraphs\n5. **Interactive demo section** (optional): &#96;\u003csection class=\"grid md:grid-cols-2 gap-8...\"\u003e&#96; with lab components\n\n## Super Simple Explanation (Core Content)\n\n| Property | Axis | What it does |\n|----------|------|--------------|\n| **justify-content** | Main axis | Spaces items along the main direction (row = horizontal, column = vertical) |\n| **align-items** | Cross axis | Aligns items within each line, perpendicular to main axis |\n| **align-content** | Cross axis | Only when there are multiple lines; spaces the lines themselves |\n\n**Simple mental model**: In a row (&#96;flex-direction: row&#96;), &#96;justify-content&#96; = left/right, &#96;align-items&#96; = top/bottom. &#96;align-content&#96; only matters when items wrap into multiple rows—it controls the gap between those rows.\n\n## Implementation Plan\n\n### 1. Create the MDX file\n\n**File**: [src/content/labs/flexbox-align.mdx](src/content/labs/flexbox-align.mdx)\n\n- **Frontmatter**: &#96;title: \"Flexbox: align-content vs justify-content vs align-items\"&#96;, &#96;description: \"A super simple guide to the three alignment properties in flexbox.\"&#96;, &#96;badge: \"CSS\"&#96;\n- **Header**: Title with inline code styling for the three properties\n- **Explanatory sections**:\n  - \"The two axes\" — main vs cross axis\n  - \"justify-content\" — main axis alignment\n  - \"align-items\" — cross axis alignment (single line)\n  - \"align-content\" — cross axis alignment (multiple lines only)\n- **Optional demo**: Either a simple &#96;FlexboxAlignDemo&#96; component or static code examples in a card\n\n### 2. Optional: FlexboxAlignDemo component\n\nIf an interactive demo is desired (to match the pattern of other labs), create [src/components/labs/FlexboxAlignDemo.tsx](src/components/labs/FlexboxAlignDemo.tsx):\n\n- Three small visual examples side-by-side or stacked, each showing one property in action\n- Use &#96;display: flex&#96;, &#96;flex-wrap: wrap&#96; where needed, and labeled containers\n- Reuse existing card styling (border, rounded, dark mode) from LayerDemo\n\n### 3. Register component in layout (if demo is added)\n\nUpdate [src/pages/l/[...slug].astro](src/pages/l/[...slug].astro) to import and pass &#96;FlexboxAlignDemo&#96; in the &#96;Content&#96; components prop.\n\n## Recommendation\n\nFor \"super simple\", the plan favors **text + static code examples** first. A minimal interactive demo (e.g., three labeled flex containers with different property values) would reinforce the concepts without adding much complexity. The css-layer post uses a two-card comparison; for flexbox we could use three small cards (one per property) or a single card with tabs/buttons to switch between examples.\n\n## Files to Create/Modify\n\n| Action | File |\n|--------|------|\n| Create | &#96;src/content/labs/flexbox-align.mdx&#96; |\n| Create (optional) | &#96;src/components/labs/FlexboxAlignDemo.tsx&#96; |\n| Edit (if demo) | &#96;src/pages/l/[...slug].astro&#96; |\n"

Here’s what was implemented:

## Summary

### 1. FlexboxAlignDemo component
**File:** [src/components/labs/FlexboxAlignDemo.tsx](src/components/labs/FlexboxAlignDemo.tsx)

- Three variants: `justify-content`, `align-items`, `align-content`
- Each variant has a dropdown to change values and a live flex container
- **justify-content**: row of items with options like flex-start, center, space-between
- **align-items**: row with items of different heights to show cross-axis alignment
- **align-content**: wrapped flex container with fixed height so multiple lines appear
- Uses the same card styling as LayerDemo (borders, dark mode, badges)

### 2. Lab post
**File:** [src/content/labs/flexbox-align.mdx](src/content/labs/flexbox-align.mdx)

- Three demo cards in a responsive grid (`md:grid-cols-3`)

### 3. Layout registration
**File:** [src/pages/l/[...slug].astro](src/pages/l/[...slug].astro)

- Imported `FlexboxAlignDemo` and passed it into the Content `components` prop

_**Agent (composer-2)**_

Updates are in place to spell out the difference between `*-items` and `*-content`:

**In the MDX (new section):**
- **`*-items`** — aligns each item within its line along the cross axis (e.g. top, center, bottom). It affects the items themselves.
- **`*-content`** — distributes extra space: either between items on the main axis, or between lines on the cross axis. It affects how leftover space is used, not the items’ size.

**In each property section:**
- `justify-content` is labeled as a **`*-content`** property.
- `align-items` is labeled as an **`*-items`** property.
- `align-content` is labeled as a **`*-content`** property.

**In the demo cards:**
- Each card’s description now starts with either `*-items` or `*-content` so the distinction is clear in the UI.

Here’s what changed in `SafeAlignmentDemo.tsx`:

### Resizable viewport
- A **range control** (96px–420px, default **140px**) sets the **same width** for both scroll areas so you’re comparing fairly.
- Width uses `min(100%, Npx)` so it still fits narrow layouts.

### Why it was hard to see before
- Both cases scrolled because the inner track is **420px** while the viewport is smaller.
- The real difference is at **`scrollLeft === 0`**: with plain **`center`**, there’s **leading empty space** before “A”; with **`safe center`**, the browser **lines “A” up with the start** (no dead space).

### Other UX tweaks
- **Scroll resets to 0** whenever you move the slider (`createEffect` + `scrollTo(0)`), so left vs safe is always compared from the same scroll position.
- A **green line** on the left marks the scroll container’s **start** so you can see whether “A” touches it.
- Short captions under each pair spell out what to look for.
- Footer note that if both look identical, the engine may not support **`safe`** yet.

Use a **narrow** viewport on the slider (around **120–160px**) to see the gap on the left in the **`center`** column and **no** gap in **`safe center`**.

Here’s what changed:

### Page layout (`safe-alignment.mdx`)
- The interactive block is now a **single column**: **Flexbox** card first, **Grid** card below (`flex flex-col gap-8` instead of `md:grid-cols-2`).

### Demo layout & behavior (`SafeAlignmentDemo.tsx`)
- The three comparisons are **stacked vertically** (no side‑by‑side columns inside the card).
- There are **three rows** with the same resizable viewport and scroll reset:
  1. **`justify-content: center`** — always shows **space before “A”** at `scrollLeft === 0` (wide inner track, narrow viewport).
  2. **`justify-content: safe center`** — real `safe` keyword; should **match row 3** when the engine supports it, **row 1** when it doesn’t.
  3. **`justify-content: start`** — **reference**: flex uses `flex-start`, grid uses `start`, so **“A” sits on the green line** every time.

So **row 1 vs row 3** always differ (center vs start). **Row 2** is the real `safe center` line, with copy explaining how to read it against rows 1 and 3.

The green start marker and short color‑coded labels (rose / amber / emerald) are unchanged in role; the footer notes flex vs grid keywords for row 3.

Here’s what was implemented:

### Cover image
- **`src/content.config.ts`** — Labs schema now uses `({ image })` and optional **`cover: image().optional()`** (same pattern as blog).
- **`src/content/labs/safe-alignment.mdx`** — `cover: /src/assets/lib/safe-grid-flex.png`.
- **`src/layouts/LabLayout.astro`** — Renders the cover with `Picture` (2:1, rounded, ring) above the lab body when `cover` is set.
- **`src/layouts/RootLayout.astro`** + **`src/components/BaseHead.astro`** — New optional **`ogCover`** so labs can set Open Graph/Twitter images **without** blog `article` metadata (`article?.cover` still wins when present).

### Demo: no scrollport
- **`SafeAlignmentDemo.tsx`** — Replaced **`overflow-x-auto`** with **`overflow-x-hidden`** (clip only). Removed refs and `createEffect` scroll resets.
- Copy now explains that **`safe`** is shown with a **clipped** viewport, not **`overflow: scroll` / `auto`**, so behavior matches layout rules better.
- **`safe-alignment.mdx`** — Short note above the demos that they use **`overflow-x: hidden`**, not a scroll container.

Other labs stay valid: **`cover`** is optional, so no frontmatter changes are required there.

---

_**User**_

combine box boxes, it's the same, grid/flex. Add the poster below the summary, and make it smaller, the same as body. Make sure to use Astro Image for loading performances.

---

Here’s what changed:

### One combined demo (`SafeAlignmentDemo.tsx`)
- Dropped the `variant` prop; there is a **single** card titled **“Flex and grid”** with one shared **viewport slider**.
- Each of the three rows (**center**, **safe center**, **start**) is a **two-column strip**: **Flex** (blue) and **Grid** (violet) with the same `justify-content` values, so the flex/grid story stays in one place.

### Poster placement & size (`safe-alignment.mdx`)
- **`Image`** from `astro:assets` plus `import safePoster from "@/assets/lib/safe-grid-flex.png"`.
- Renders **right under the header summary** (after the intro `<p>`, before the main article `<section>`).
- Wrapped in **`max-w-3xl mx-auto`** so it matches the **body column** width, with modest **`widths={[360, 540, 720, 900]}`** and **`sizes="(max-width: 48rem) 100vw, 48rem"`** for responsive srcset, **`loading="eager"`** (above the fold), **`decoding="async"`**, and light border/shadow.

### Lab layout (`LabLayout.astro`)
- Removed the large top **`Picture`**; the page no longer shows a duplicate hero.
- **`ogCover={entry.data.cover}`** is unchanged so **Open Graph** still uses the same asset from frontmatter.

Frontmatter **`cover: /src/assets/lib/safe-grid-flex.png`** stays for SEO; the visible poster is the optimized **`Image`** in the MDX body.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_

You were right — it was a demo logic issue, not just styling.

I changed the demo so `safe` is evaluated in the **actual alignment container**:

- The flex/grid boxes themselves are now the narrow containers.
- Items overflow those containers directly (with `overflow-x: hidden`), instead of overflowing an inner wrapper.
- Row 1 is now explicit **`unsafe center`**.
- Row 2 is **`safe center`**.
- Row 3 remains **start reference** (`flex-start` / `start`).

This is the correct condition where `safe` can differ from unsafe/center.  
Build passes and lints are clean.

If your browser still renders row 2 exactly like row 1, that indicates runtime support for this overflow-position behavior is missing/partial in that engine version.

---

_**User**_

but there shouldn't be any scroll?

---

_**Agent (composer-2)**_

Correct — there should be **no scroll** in this demo.

It now uses `overflow-x: hidden` on the demo boxes, so overflow is clipped (not scrollable).  
If you still see scrolling, it likely means one of these:

- you’re seeing a cached old client bundle
- page-level/container overflow from elsewhere is being interpreted as demo scroll
- browser extension/custom CSS is altering overflow behavior

If you want, I can make it extra explicit by also adding `overflow-y-hidden` and a hard `overscroll-behavior: contain` on the demo boxes.

Here’s what was implemented:

### Schema & content
- Renamed **`created_date` → `published_date`** in the labs collection (`src/content.config.ts`).
- Updated all lab frontmatter: `safe-alignment`, `flexbox-align`, `css-layer`, `interpolate-size`.
- Renamed the sort helper to **`sortLabsByPublishedDate`** (`src/functions.ts`) and wired it on the home and `/labs` pages.

### Visible date
- **`LabLayout.astro`**: centered published line above the lab body, using **`FormattedDate`** and the same **`sr-only` “Published at”** pattern as posts (`layouts.postLayout.publishedAt`).
- **`/labs`** and **home** lab cards: show the published date above the description.

### SEO
- **`BaseHead.astro`**: new optional **`publishedDocument`** (`publishedTime`, optional `modifiedTime`, optional `authors`).
- When `publishedDocument` is set (or blog `article` is set), Open Graph uses **`og:type: article`** and **`article.publishedTime` / `modifiedTime` / `authors` / `tags`**.
- Extra **`<meta property="article:published_time">`** (and **`modified_time`** when present) for crawlers.
- **`LabLayout`**: **`TechArticle`** JSON-LD with **`datePublished`**, **`headline`**, **`description`**, **`mainEntityOfPage`**, and optional **`author`** (default site author).

**`RootLayout`** passes **`publishedDocument`** through to **`BaseHead`**.

New labs should set **`published_date`** in frontmatter (same YAML date style as before). Build completes successfully.

_**Agent (composer-2)**_



Here’s what was going on and what changed:

### Already in place
Labs with **`cover:`** in frontmatter were already passed as **`ogCover`** from `LabLayout` → `RootLayout` → `BaseHead`, and `getImage()` was used for the social image. So the poster file in frontmatter was already intended to be the OG image.

### What was wrong / improved
1. **Twitter card** – Tags were only set when **`twitterCreator`** existed, so many lab shares had **no** `twitter:image`. Twitter now always gets **`summary_large_image`** with **title, description, and image**; **`creator`** is optional.
2. **Absolute URLs** – Open Graph and Twitter now use a resolved **`ogImageAbsoluteUrl`** (from `Astro.site` when `src` is site-relative), which avoids broken previews on some platforms.
3. **Structured data** – When a lab has **`cover`**, **`TechArticle`** JSON-LD now includes **`image`** with that same optimized, absolute URL (aligned with the OG poster).

**Reminder:** The in-page poster and OG image both come from the same asset as long as **`cover:`** in the lab frontmatter points at it (as with `safe-alignment`). If you drop `cover` and only import the image in MDX, OG will fall back to the default avatar unless you add `cover` back.
